label: Original-phase input of n/j/u/h/1/2/k/p/z/f/r (first occurrence, t>=2), boosted by earlier t/y/v/s/k/w
explanation: Fires only while the original sequence is being read (93% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (7%); it never fires in the copy phase and almost never at t=0-1. Rates peak at t=3-5 and fall off by t=8-9. It is driven mainly by the identity of the current input token: n is strongest (23% rate, 18% of mass), followed by j, u, h, 1, 2, k, p, and more weakly z, f, r. Mostly first occurrences (in_first=1 holds 93% of mass). The token signal is gated by context: it is much stronger when y, t, v, s, k or w appeared earlier (first_tok y/t and prev2_tok t have the highest lift). The largest activations are n/j/u/h at t=3-5 in sequences starting with y t. Weaker carry-over activations show up on the tokens and the <DEL> right after a trigger. The single predicate gets dev F1 0.56 with mass recall 0.73; the response looks graded across token and context rather than a clean boolean, so precision stays low (many trigger tokens without enough context stay inactive).
